dailyQuestions.tex: If $\underset{x\to a}{Lt}f(x)=\ell(\ne0)$ then prove that in a deleted neighbourhood of $a$, $f$ keeps the same sign as that of $\ell$.
Prove that every monotone decreasing sequence which is bounded below is convergent and converges to its greatest lower bound.
Prove that a sequence of real numbers is convergent iff it is a Cauchy sequence.
Find the equations of the generators of the hyperboloid $x^2+y^2-4z^2=9$ passing through the point $(-3,4,2)$.
Find total length of perimeter of the cardioid \(r=a(1+\cos\theta)\).
Solve the nonlinear differential equation \(y^2\log(y)=xyp+p^2\).

When a function \(f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R\) is said to be of bounded variation? If \(f,g\) be two functions of bounded variation over \([a,b]\) then prove that \(f-g\) and \(fg\) are of bounded variation on \([a,b]\).
Solve the partial differential equation $x^3(y-z)p+y^3(z-x)q+z^3(y-x)=0$.

A particle moves with a central acceleration $\mu(r+\frac{a^4}{r^3})$ being projected from an apse at a distance $a$ with a velocity $2\sqrt\mu a$. Prove that it describes the curve $r^2(2+\cos\sqrt3\theta)=3a^2$.

dailyQuestions.title: Linear Programming Problem and Numerical Methods

dailyQuestions.tex:
From the following values of $x$ and $f(x)$
\[\begin{array}{c|rrrrrr}x&0.20&0.22&0.24&0.26&0.28&0.30\\\hline f(x)&1.6596&1.6698&1.6804&1.6912&1.7024&1.7139\end{array}\]
calculate the value of $f(0.23)$ by using Newton's forward interpolation formula.
State and prove Mean Value Theorem for a function of two variables.
Describe the regula falsi method for computing a simple root of an equation $f(x)=0$. Also find the condition of convergence of this method, if there be any.
Prove that if the density of a liquid at rest under gravity varies as the square root of the pressure, the density increases uniformly with the depth.
Define (i) Simple hypothesis, (ii) Composite hypothesis, and (iii) Null hypothesis and give examples of each of them.

The marks obtained by 18 candidates in an examination have a mean 56 and variance 65. Find 95\% confidence interval for the mean of the population of marks, assuming it to be normal. Given that for 17 degrees of freedom, $P(|t|>2.11)=0.05$.

dailyQuestions.title: Linear Programming Problem, Game Theory and Mathematical Statistics

dailyQuestions.tex: Prove that the maximum likelihood estimate of the parameter $\alpha$ of a population having density function $f(x)=2(\alpha-x)/\alpha^2$ ($0<x<\alpha$) for a sample of unit size is $2x$, $x$ being the sample value, and examine whether the estimate is biased or unbiased.

Write a Fortran program to calculate the monthly telephone bill at the following rates:
\par First 300 calls : no charges
\par Calls between 301 and 501: at the rate of 50p per call
\par Calls between 501 and 1000: at the rate of 80p per call
\par Calls more than 1000: at the rate of Rs. 1.5 per call
\par and rental charges of Rs. 75 per month.
Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity 1. Then show that every proper ideal of $R$ is contained in a maximal ideal of $R$.
Let $f$ be an entire function such that $f(z)=u(y)+iv(x)$. Show that $f$ can be expressed as $f(z)=az+b$, for some $a,b\in\mathbb C$ with $\operatorname{Re}(a)=0$.
Define covariant derivative. Show that covariant derivative of a tensor is again a tensor. Find covariant derivative of a mixed tensor of rank 5, contravariant of order 2 and covariant of order 3.
Show that if a sequence $\{x_n\}$ converges, then it is a Cauchy sequence. Is converse of this true? Justify your answer.

If the Dirichlet problem for a bounded region has a solution, then it is unique whereas if the Neumann problem for a bounded region has a solution, then it is either unique or it differs from the one another by a constant only -- prove it.
State Cauchy's residue theorem. Using this theorem evaluate $\displaystyle\oint_{|z|=\frac32}\frac{z-1}{z^2+2z}dz$.
Show that a linear operator $T:V\longrightarrow V$ is triangulizable if and only if the characteristic polynomial of $T$ splits into linear factors.

Describe the notion of convergence in measure. If a sequence $\{f_n\}$ of measurable functions on a set $E$ converges in measure to a measurable function $f$ on $E$ and each $f_n$ and $f$ are finite a.e. on $E$, show that there exists a subsequence $\{f_{n_k}\}$ which converges to $f$ pointwise a.e. on $E$.

Determine the coefficients in the formula
\[
\int_0^{2h}x^{-1/2}f(x)dx=(2h)^{1/2}[a_0f(0)+a_1f(h)+a_2f(2h)]+R
\]
and calculate the remainder $R$, when $f'''(x)$ is constant.

Let $X=\{a,b,c,d\}$ and\par
\[\tau=\{\emptyset,X,\{a\},\{a,b\},\{a,c\},\{a,b,c\}\}.\]
Show that $\tau$ is a topology on $X$. Also determine whether $(X,\tau)$ is normal.
Show that the specific enthalpy for moist air is approximately given by $I=C_pT+\mu'L+$constant, whether the air is saturated or not.
Find the singularities of the function $f(z)=\tan\dfrac1z$ and determine the nature of it.

Find the fourth order accurate discretized form of first order partial derivative with respect to one independent variable using the values of the dependent variable at the $(i+2,j),(i+1,j),(i-1,j)$ and $(i-2,j)$ points.

Use resolution to show the validity of the following argument: \par
Custom officials searched everyone who entered this country who was not a V.I.P. Some of the drug-pushers entered this country and they were only searched by drug-pushers. No drug-pusher was a V.I.P. Therefore, some officials were drug-pushers.

Check whether the ellipsoid $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2e^t\sin\left(\frac\pi4+t\right)}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2e^t\cos\left(\frac\pi4+t\right)}+\dfrac{z^2}{c^2\sec2t}=1$ is a possible form of boundary surface of a liquid at any time $t$. Find the normal velocity of the boundary, if it is a boundary surface.
Discuss the motion of a charged particle under constant electric ($\mathbf E$) and magnetic ($\mathbf B$) fields. Hence define the $\mathbf E\times\mathbf B$-drift velocity of the charged particle.
Use Hirota's Bilinear method to obtain the two-soliton solution of the KdV equation.
Formulate a mathematical model for study of the physiological problem of brain injury, when the head is subjected to impulsive load.
Formulate a mathematical model for study of the physiological problem of brain injury, when the head is subjected to rotational acceleration.
Write a program in MATLAB to solve the following coupled nonlinear equations: $x=y+\cos(x+y)$, $y=x+\sin(xy)$.

Solve the following NLPP graphically:
\[\begin{aligned}\text{Maximize }f(x_1,x_2)&=2x_1+3x_2-x_1^2\\
\text{subject to }x_1+2x_2&\le4,\\x_1,x_2&\ge0.\end{aligned}\]
Let $\alpha$ be a root of $1+x+x^3\in F_2[x]$, and let $C$ be the binary BCH code of length 7 with designed distance 4 generated by $g(x)=\mathit{lcm}(M^0(x),M^1(x),M^2(x))$. Find $d(C)$.

dailyQuestions.title: Differential Equations II and Dynamics of a Particle

dailyQuestions.tex: Derive the equation of motion for a particle moving on a plane under the action of a force proportional to the distance of the particle from a fixed point on the plane.

In a simple harmonic motion, the distance of a particle from the middle point of its path in three consecutive seconds are $x,y$ and $z$. Show the time of a complete oscillation is $2\pi/\cos^{-1}(\frac{x+z}{2y})$.
For the binomial $(n,p)$ distribution, prove that $\mu_{k+1}=p(1-p)\left(nk\mu_{k-1}+\frac{d\mu_k}{dp}\right)$, and hence obtain $\gamma_1$.

Let $f(z)$ be analytic within and on a simple closed curve $C$ except for a finite number of poles within $C$ and let $f(z)\neq0$ anywhere on $C$. Then prove that\\$\dfrac{1}{2\pi}\Delta_C\arg f(z)=\dfrac{1}{2\pi i}\displaystyle\oint_C\frac{f'(z)}{f(z)}\,dz=Z-P$, where $Z$ and $P$ respectively denote the number of zeros and poles of $f(z)$ within $C$, a zero or pole of order $m$ being counted $m$ times.

Discuss the shooting method for solving the boundary value problem\\$-u''+p(x)u'+q(x)u(x)=r(x),\ a<x<b$\\subject to the conditions $u(a)=\gamma$, $u(b)=\gamma_2$ where $p(x)$, $q(x)$ and $r(x)$ are assumed to be continuous in $[a,b]$ and $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$ are non-zero constants.

Which of the following are true?
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
        \item If $X_1$ and $X_2$ are independent uniform $(0,1)$ then $X_1 + X_2$ is uniform $(0,2)$
        \item If $X$ is uniform $(0, n)$ then $X / n$ is uniform $(0,1)$
        \item If $X_1$ and $X_2$ are standard normal, then $(X_1 + X_2) / \sqrt{2}$ is standard normal
        \item If $X$ is exponential with mean 1, then $e^{-X}$ is uniform $(0,1)$
    \end{enumerate}

Which of the following are class equations for a finite group?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item $1 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 13 + 13 = 39$
\item $1 + 1 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 14$
\item $1 + 3 + 3 + 7 + 7 = 21$
\item $1 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 5 + 5 = 15$
\end{enumerate}

Consider the set $A=\{x \in \mathbb{Q}: 0<(\sqrt{2}-1) x<\sqrt{2}+1\}$ as a subset of $\mathbb{R}$. Which of the following statements is true?
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
    \item   $\sup A=2+2 \sqrt{3}$
    \item   $\sup A=3+2 \sqrt{2}$
    \item   $\inf A=2+2 \sqrt{3}$
    \item   $\inf A=3+2 \sqrt{2}$
\end{enumerate}

Let $v_1, v_2, v_3, v_4, v_5$, and $v_6$ be six distinct vectors in a vector space. There are $\binom{6}{4} = 15$ distinct subsets consisting precisely of four of these vectors. Suppose that, out of these $15$ subsets, only $\{v_1, v_2, v_3, v_4\}$ and $\{v_1, v_2, v_3, v_5\}$ are linearly independent, and the remaining $13$ are linearly dependent. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
  \item $v_6$ is the zero vector.
  \item $v_4$ and $v_5$ are non-zero scalar multiples of each other.
\end{enumerate}
